chunks: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a concubine (umm al-walad) who belongs to a man, and he has already sent her on pilgrimage: does that count for her as the Hajj of Islam? He said, 'No.' I asked, 'Does she have a reward in her Hajj?' He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.أَحَجَّهَا: He sent her on pilgrimage / He performed Hajj for her
key_terms.أُمِّ الْوَلَدِ: Concubine (female slave who bears her master's child)

ai.seo_question: Does a master's payment for a concubine's Hajj count as her obligatory duty?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that while a concubine (Umm al-Walad) sent by her master fulfills her specific obligation of Hajj al-Islam, the act is not considered valid if it is merely a delegation without her personal volition or if the master's intent was solely to discharge his duty. Nevertheless, she accrues spiritual reward (Ajr) for the pilgrimage, highlighting the distinction between legal validity (Ijab) and spiritual merit in Shia jurisprudence.
